title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 421
paragraphs: and after this they saw last of all their receptacles for dead bodies, which are said to be made of crystal in the following way. When they have dried the corpse, whether by the Egyptian method or by some other, they cover it entirely with plaster and then adorn it with painting, making the figure resemble the living man as closely as possible. After this they place around it a block of crystal hollowed out, for they dig this up in great quantities, and it is very easy to work. The dead body, being in the middle of the block, is visible through it, but produces no unpleasant smell nor any other unseemly effect, and all its parts are visible, just like the dead body itself. For a year the nearest relatives keep the block in their house, giving the dead man the first share of everything and offering him sacrifices; and after this period they carry it out and set it up around the city.
